data_fields.name: respawn_base_min_minutes
data_fields.donor_constant: NPC_MIN_RESPAWN_INTERVAL, default 5 (minutes or game minutes, see note)

data_fields.name: respawn_spread_minutes
data_fields.donor_constant: 5 (Util.Random(min, min + 5)) (minutes or game minutes, see note)

data_fields.name: respawn_named_bonus_minutes
data_fields.donor_constant: 5 when name has a capital letter (minutes or game minutes, see note)

data_fields.name: respawn_level_add_per_level
data_fields.donor_constant: (Level - 65) + NPC_MIN_RESPAWN_INTERVAL, in minutes (minutes or game minutes, see note)

data_fields.name: respawn_explicit_value
data_fields.donor_constant: stored seconds x 1000; -1 = default; negative = never (minutes or game minutes, see note)

best_idea: A dead mob's respawn is a per-mob timer whose delay is drawn from a tiered band (named mobs get extra minutes, realm mobs a fixed short band, higher levels a level add-on) and held in a region-wide pending registry; the spawn refuses to run if the mob is alive.
decision_why: Tiered respawn bands and a pending registry fit zone respawn as data on the server, but the donor has no population cap, despawn or grace timer and re-draws delays on resync, so Frankendom must store the due time and take caps from row 23.
acceptance: A server test kills a seeded mob and asserts its respawn delay falls in the zone's band for its tier (named plus 5 minutes, realm 5 to 10 minutes), that a resync re-arms each pending respawn with its remaining time, and that a spawn call on a live mob is refused; in play a killed zone mob returns at its spawn point after the tier delay at full health.
